translations.literal: and sent [him] to the pale, cloud-covered, darkness-overspread places of Orcus, of death
translations.note: Orcus is the underworld. The phrasing seems to echo the old Latin verse 'pallida leti, nubila tenebris loca' ('pale places of death, clouded with darkness'), which Cicero quotes in the Tusculan Disputations as a line of early Roman tragedy. Burton has reworked it ('obnubila', 'obsita'), so the identification is not certain.
